lesson.label: 📖 Bài học chính
lesson.title: 1. Can I get a second opinion?
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Mia has a presentation with a new client tomorrow. She asks her colleague, Tom, to look at her slides.*
lines: Tom, have you got five minutes? Could you **have a quick look at** my slides for tomorrow? I'd really like **a second opinion**.
And please **be honest**. **I'd rather hear it from you than** from the client.
**Fair enough.** OK, **first of all**, the design looks great. It's clean and professional, and the charts are really **easy to follow**.
**Yeah, it shows. The only thing is**, some of the slides have **too much on them**. This one has a whole paragraph. I think the client might **stop listening**.
Yeah, **I was worried about** that one. **What would you do?**
**Maybe you could cut it down to** three bullet points and explain the rest **out loud**. **That way**, they'll **focus on** you, not on the screen.
Hmm, the ending is **a bit sudden**. You go straight from the prices to "Thank you." **It might be worth** adding one slide with **the main points**, so the client remembers them.
**Good point. I hadn't thought of that.**
But **overall**, it's really good. The part about delivery times is **spot on**. That's exactly what the client cares about.
**That's really helpful**, thanks. I'll **make a few changes** tonight and practise it one more time.
Sounds good. You'll be fine. Good luck tomorrow!

lesson.title: 2. The monthly one-to-one
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Sam has worked in the marketing team for six months. His manager, Laura, is having their monthly one-to-one meeting with him.*
lines: So, **how are things going** at the moment?
Pretty good, thanks. It's been **a busy month**, but I'm enjoying it.
**Good to hear. I wanted to start by saying** you've **done a great job on** the social media campaign. A lot more people follow our page now, since you **took over**.
Thanks, that's really nice to hear.

**There's one thing I wanted to mention, though.** Your last two weekly reports were a few days late. **It's not a big problem**, but it **slows down** the rest of the team, because they need your numbers for their own reports.
Oh, right. Sorry about that. To be honest, I've been **swamped** since the campaign started.
**I understand.** You've **got a lot on your plate** right now. Is there anything that would help?
Maybe if I knew **the most important tasks** earlier in the week? Sometimes urgent work **comes up** on Thursday, and then I **fall behind** with everything else.
**That's fair.** I'll send you a list of **priorities** every Monday morning. And if you think you **can't meet a deadline**, just **give me a heads-up**. We can always **work something out.**
That would really help. I'll make sure I **let you know** early **from now on**.
Great. And **just so you know**, I'm really happy with your work **overall**. This is just a small thing.
Of course. Let's **check in** again next month and **see how it's going**.

homework.title: Part 3: Listening
homework.intro: Leo has just finished his first week as a waiter at a busy restaurant. The manager, Kate, talks to him at the end of his shift. Listen to the conversation, then do Parts A and B.

script.text: Leo, have you got a minute before you go?
I just wanted to say you've done a great job this week. The customers really like you. Two of them said ==you were very friendly==.
Really? Thanks! That's nice to hear.
There's one thing I wanted to mention, though. ==Sometimes you don't write the orders down.== Yesterday, ==table six got the wrong drinks==.
Oh, I'm sorry about that. ==I thought I could remember everything==, but it was really busy.
I understand. Friday nights are crazy. It's not a big problem, but it confuses the kitchen. Maybe you could always use your ==notebook==, even for small orders.
That makes sense. I'll do that from now on.
Great. And one more thing. When customers are waiting for a table, try to tell them ==how long== it will be. ==People don't mind waiting if they know how long.==
Good point. I didn't think of that.
But overall, ==I'm really happy with you==. You learn fast.
Thanks, Kate. I appreciate the feedback.
